items.text: Hey Nephilim,
Patch 1.1 is now live!
We’re excited to bring you our first major update for Crimson Moon, with new ways to play, new challenges to take on, new rewards to discover, and a huge range of improvements across the game.

Patch 1.1 introduces 6-Skull Difficulty, the new Omens system, Leaderboards, new Boons, new Trinkets and a new reward to discover in the Hub. We’ve also introduced a new save system, controller remapping and a range of quality-of-life improvements, alongside another substantial round of fixes across the game.
And this is just the beginning. We’re excited to continue building on Crimson Moon, expanding the experience and giving you more reasons to return to Gildenarch.

Team Metal is incredibly appreciative of the passion and support this community continues to show for Crimson Moon. Your feedback continues to help shape the work we’re doing, and we cannot thank you enough for being part of this journey with us.

On a more personal note, thank you for allowing us to share a lifelong dream of ours with you. Seeing this community form around Crimson Moon, hearing your stories and watching you experience the world we’ve created means more to the team than we can adequately put into words.
6-Skull Difficulty: You have just one life. Can you survive?
Omens: Take on 7 new difficulty modifiers that give you more ways to change the challenge of your runs.
Leaderboards: Put your skills to the test and see how you stack up against other Nephilim across every mission and difficulty level.

New Boons and Trinkets: Discover 12 new Boons and 12 new Trinkets throughout Gildenarch. We’ve also introduced the ability to re-roll Boons at Nexus Gates and at Mereda (in the Hub), giving you more options during your run.
A New Reward: There’s a new reward chest waiting for you in the Hub; we’ll leave the rest for you to discover... 👀
Quality-of-Life Improvements: Controller button remapping, clearer Quest XP information, and further improvements across the HUD, menus and controls.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45986190/e9110156f2a4562be15eceee0a7660b51ab2dc43.jpg"]
Alongside everything new, we’ve continued working through the issues you’ve been reporting since launch.

notes.title: Some of the biggest improvements in Patch 1.1 include

items.text: A new save system, designed to address various issues that could cause players to lose progress.
Further co-op and multiplayer fixes, including progression, Quick Match, crossplay, joining games and combat.
Fixes for issues preventing Relic Quests and other objectives from progressing correctly.
Further fixes across combat, Boons and Weapon Arts, including issues with effects, status effects and Boons not behaving as intended.
Further performance and stability improvements across PC, consoles and Steam Deck.
Patch 1.1 includes over 300 fixes and a whole range of improvements across Crimson Moon, including co-op and multiplayer, combat, quests and progression, equipment, performance, UI and more.
For the complete list of changes, check out the full Patch 1.1 notes here.
Patch 1.1 marks an exciting step forward for Crimson Moon, and the team is already hard at work on what comes next.
We’re not quite ready to share the details just yet, but there are more new experiences coming to Gildenarch, and we can’t wait to show you what we’ve been working on.

items.text: Hey Nephilim,
Hotfix 1.0.2 is now live on all platforms!

Team Metal has been hard at work addressing as many of the issues reported by players as possible. This is our biggest update yet, with hundreds of fixes and improvements across saves and progression, co-op, combat, Boons and Weapon Arts, crashes, performance, camera and much more.

Thank you to everyone who has continued to report issues and share feedback with us. Your reports continue to help the team identify, reproduce and prioritise issues, and many of the fixes included below directly address issues raised by the community.
There’s a lot in this update. Here are just some of the highlights:
Major co-op fixes, including issues with Quickplay, joining games, progression, dealing damage and parrying, alongside several issues that could leave players stuck or unable to continue.
More save and progression fixes, including issues where progress and unlock information could incorrectly carry between different save files, alongside improvements to make overwriting saves safer.
Lore Scrolls can now be collected in co-op, fixing an issue that could prevent the second player from collecting them and progressing related quests.
Clear the Area objectives should now be more reliable, with fixes for enemies that could fail to spawn or make their way towards you, preventing you from completing the objective.
Fixed numerous locations where players could become stuck in the environment or fall through the world.
Lots of fixes for Boons and Weapon Arts, including Angelic Bulwark, Brewmaster, Aftershock Technique, Avenging Pestilence, Shield of Many, Pyromancer, Impaling Throw and more.
Improved the downed and revive experience in co-op, fixing several issues that could occur while players were downed or being revived.
More crash and performance fixes across PC and consoles, including improvements across multiple levels and boss encounters.
Steam Deck improvements, including fixes for controls, UI readability, combat desync and performance.
More camera and lock-on fixes, including issues during rolling attacks and encounters with Egregore and Demon Brute.
Clearer Status Effect information for Rage, Poisoned, Freeze, Marked and Sundered.
Improved loot and Gold pickups, including a fix for dropped items bunching together and a new setting that allows you to auto-pickup Gold!
Plus many more fixes across quests, UI, localisation, audio, cinematics, enemies, bosses and the world itself.
We know save and progression loss has been one of the biggest concerns for players, and it continues to be one of our highest priorities.

Hotfix 1.0.2 includes a number of important save fixes designed to make saves more stable and secure, addressing several of the issues we’ve identified through player reports and our ongoing investigation.

While we expect these changes to make a meaningful improvement to save stability, our work here isn’t finished. A few of the remaining save issues are more complex, and for Patch 1.1 we’re planning a more substantial rework of how saves are handled. This is a larger piece of work that requires additional development and testing, but will allow us to fix the underlying issues and better protect your saves going forward.

Many of the remaining save issues we’re investigating occur when moving between devices, so in the meantime, we recommend playing Crimson Moon on a single device where possible. Until we can confirm these issues are fully resolved, we recommend avoiding switching devices when playing the same save.
For players on PC, you may also want to create a local backup of your save as an additional precaution while we continue this work.

We know this isn’t an ideal recommendation, but we want to be transparent about the current situation while also making clear that 1.0.2 contains meaningful improvements to save stability. Please continue reporting any save or progression issues you experience after updating - your reports are incredibly valuable as we continue this work.
Hotfix 1.0.2 is another substantial step forward for Crimson Moon, but our work doesn’t stop here.

Our next major update, Patch 1.1, is planned for October. Alongside the wider work on saves outlined above, 1.1 will focus on further quality-of-life improvements, including gear and Blacksmith improvements, clearer gear and Boon information, better visibility of run progression, rewards and unlocks, further control remapping improvements, and additional co-op improvements.
And while our focus since launch has understandably been on fixing and improving the core experience, we’re also looking further ahead.
There’s more coming to Crimson Moon.

As we move into October, we’ll begin sharing more about new content coming to the game and what’s next for Gildenarch. We’re not quite ready to reveal everything just yet, but you won’t have to wait too much longer to find out more.
For now, there are a lot more fixes to dig into below.
Crashes & Stability

Since launch, we’ve been listening closely to your feedback and bug reports, and the team has been taking action on the issues having the biggest impact on players.

Hotfix 1.0.1 is the first of several updates we're working on and includes fixes and improvements for camera and lock-on behaviour, save and progression issues, crashes, Steam Deck/PC save syncing, co-op, PC keybinding improvements, HUD scaling, and more.

We know that save and progression loss has been one of the most serious issues affecting some players, and addressing it continues to be a top priority for the team. With this update, we've added rolling backup saves to provide additional protection if a save becomes corrupted or fails to load, alongside fixes for several instances where player progression could be unintentionally reset. We've also fixed an issue affecting save syncing between Steam Deck and PC, while we continue to investigate further reports of save and progression loss.

Thank you to everyone who has reported an issue or shared feedback. Your reports, videos, and additional details are directly helping the team investigate, prioritise, and take action on the issues affecting players most.
For a quick overview, here are some of the biggest issues addressed in this update:
Camera & Lock-On Improvements - Improved lock-on camera behaviour for large stationary bosses, with additional improvements to camera behaviour around large and elite enemies.
Crash & Stability Fixes - Fixed several crashes across PC and console, including a crash during the Egregore boss fight.
Steam Deck to PC Save Sync - Fixed an issue affecting save syncing when playing on Steam Deck and PC using the same Steam account.

Co-op Fixes - Addressed issues with co-op invites, hosting after reconnecting, additional disconnect handling, and players not being revived correctly at activated Nexus Gates. Co-op run progress will now also persist for clients, allowing them to continue the run solo.
HUD Scaling and Fixes - Added HUD scaling options and improved UI scaling at 4K resolutions.
PC Keybinding Improvements - Fixed several issues affecting custom keybindings, prompts, and HUD icons.
You can find the full list of fixes and improvements below.
Fixed a number of crashes across Steam, Epic Games Store, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam Deck, including a crash that could occur during the Egregore boss fight.
Fixed various Co-op desync issues
Improved the lock-on camera when fighting large stationary bosses, including Tyrigon and the Dry Rot King’s God form.
Made additional improvements to lock-on camera behaviour around large and elite enemies, reducing some instances of unwanted camera movement and laying the groundwork for further improvements.

Patch 1.0.0.1 has passed testing and we've decided to put our Alpha implementation of keybinding support into your hands now, rather than make you wait for the full, polished version.
The update is available now (version 162350), giving PC players basic keyboard & mouse remapping and mouse sensitivity controls while we continue to refine and expand the feature.

Keybinding support was already planned for PC, but we chose to hold the initial implementation at launch while we resolved some remaining issues. Your feedback reinforced that getting these options into your hands should be a priority, so the team has been working to get them ready as quickly as possible.

IMPORTANT NOTE: this is our first Alpha implementation of keybinding support, not the final, polished experience we intend to deliver. You can find this new feature under the Settings Menu > Keyboard > select the custom keyboard profile (click the left arrow).
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45986190/29711306af436116bfcc73df51f663c5e7b152e0.png"]

Right now, you can rebind all available actions, revert bindings to their defaults and adjust mouse sensitivity, but there are some things not included in this version that we're working to add in a future update – these include:
Multiple bindings - assign more than one key to the same action
Double-tap inputs - assign actions to quickly pressing a key twice
Hold inputs - assign actions to holding a key down

We made the decision to get this Alpha functionality into your hands sooner rather than make you wait for the full implementation. This is only our first step, and we want your feedback to help us refine what comes next and what's important to you.
Please let us know what works, what doesn’t, and any issues you encounter. We’d also love to hear what additional keybinding options or functionality you’d like to see in the next implementation.
We’ll continue refining and expanding keybinding support in future updates.

Our attention is also firmly on the other pressing issues players have raised since launch, including camera improvements, progression loss, UI scaling settings and improvements, game crashes & additional controller layout options.
The team is actively working through these now, and we’ll have more to share on the next patch soon.
We won’t keep you waiting long ⚔️
